source_user: Choose between tensor and pipeline parallelism for a latency-sensitive multi-GPU service. State the assumptions needed. Scenario variant 247: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: compare per-GPU memory, communication topology, layer partitioning, batch and microbatch behavior, synchronization, latency target, and failure/reconfiguration costs.
corrected_answer: Scenario variant 2446: do not select tensor parallelism (TP) or pipeline parallelism (PP) from the prompt alone. Assume the model graph and layer shapes, precision, parameter and activation memory, GPU count/type and usable HBM (GiB), topology/link bandwidth, software versions, clocks, request lengths, arrival rate, concurrency, batching policy, and explicit latency, throughput, error, quality, and availability SLOs are known; label estimates versus measured facts. Enumerate topology-aware TP degrees and balanced PP stage partitions, rejecting any candidate lacking positive memory headroom or a feasible reconfiguration plan. Hypothesis: on identical hardware and a representative fixed workload, the feasible candidate with lower held-out p99 end-to-end latency while meeting every SLO gate is superior; falsify this if p99 is not lower or any gate fails. Warm up, randomize paired trials, tune only on disjoint data, then evaluate held-out requests while holding workload mix, arrival rate, precision, clocks, concurrency, and batch policy constant. Measure per-GPU memory/headroom, compute time, TP collective or PP activation-transfer time, synchronization wait, stage imbalance, pipeline bubbles, queueing, throughput, TTFT, TPOT, p50/p95/p99 latency, errors, quality, availability, and recovery time, all with units and uncertainty. Control for kernel/compiler versions, placement, thermal state, retries, stragglers, request mix, and warm-up; use a fixed seed and report sample sizes and confidence intervals. Test microbatch and batch-size effects separately because PP bubbles and TP collectives scale differently. Run fault injection only with authorization and isolation, then verify restart, state consistency, degraded-mode behavior, and recovery time. Canary the winner with an automatic SLO guard, shadow traffic where possible, and roll back to the last known-good configuration on any gate violation, error increase, quality regression, memory pressure, or recovery failure. If data are insufficient, keep the current configuration and mark the choice unresolved rather than inventing a platform-specific winner.
risks: Missing platform facts and SLO thresholds prevent a universal TP/PP winner.
Tail latency is sensitive to batching, queueing, stage imbalance, collectives, stragglers, retries, and workload drift.
Unauthorized fault testing or canaries can disrupt service.
evidence_required: Per-GPU memory/headroom and topology measurements for feasible TP/PP configurations and partitions.
Repeated randomized paired trials with disjoint tuning and held-out p50/p95/p99, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, error, quality, and availability results.
Authorized canary, recovery, rollback rehearsal, and domain-expert review.
